The previous description and admission requirements were reflective of our former Master of Science Specializing in Developmental Science program that no longer exists.
In addition, we propose allowing two options to complete the Couple and Family Therapy specialization: the capstone option (already approved) and the thesis option (a new option).
For those in the capstone option, there are no changes as the capstone is completed in HDF 581 in the final semester which is already a part of the program.
For those wanting to complete a thesis, we propose allowing the student to complete the thesis upon enrolling in and successfully completing a minimum 6 credits of HDF 599 and a successful thesis defense.
We propose this to be fully optional for each student enrolled in the CFT specialization.

For students who select this graduation pathway, they would be required to take additional coursework (HDF 599); although in some cases, some of these credits could overlap with student electives.
We anticipate students would take 60 credits (existing requirement for all students) in the capstone option; those who select the thesis option would take between 63-66 credits depending on their elective choices.
These changes are reflected in the specialization-level proposal for CFT.

Online - Academic Year Summer 2026 Fall 2026 The Graduate Certificate in Leadership for Sports Management (12 credits) is designed for professionals who are moving into or occupying management roles in sports who seek to develop the strategic leadership, business acumen, and inclusive mindset required to thrive in today’s dynamic sport industry.
Through a flexible format where courses are available online, in person, or students can flex between formats, this certificate blends core leadership development with sports-specific business skills.
Students will explore sport as a dynamic venue for social equity, brand-building, revenue generation, and community partnership, while strengthening their capacity to lead diverse teams, shape culture, and drive organizational transformation.
On completion, graduates will be prepared to apply leadership strategies, ethically navigate sport management challenges, and promote inclusive and sustainable sports organizations at the local, national or global level.
Program Requirements Students must complete all required courses and one elective course from the approved list below.

Required Courses (9 credits): BUS532 - Leadership BUS582 - Global Sporting Events Management BUS570 - Sports Marketing Elective Courses (choose at least one, 3 credits): BUS506 - Operations and Project Management BUS509 - Law and Ethics BUS515 - Innovation and Entrepreneurship Practicum BUS577 - Sports Analytics EDC560 - Group Procedures and Leadership EDC 576 - Diversity and Cultural Competence in Student Affairs MBA524 - Entrepreneurship and Innovation MBA593 - Business Internship Other course with director approval Is this program offered in the accelerated online calendar? By the end of the certificate, students will be able to: 1.
Apply leadership theories and self ‐ assessment to develop a clear leadership style suited to sports organizations. 2.
Evaluate and implement business and marketing strategies relevant to sports organizations. 3.
Demonstrate cultural competency and inclusive leadership.
This certificate supports the institution’s mission of fostering transformative leadership, innovation and societal impact.
It aligns with our emphasis on experience economy, purpose-driven business, and sustainable outcomes, by positioning sport organizations as engines of community engagement, brand development, social justice, and economic vitality.
In particular, at a coastal-region institution (e.g., in Rhode Island/New England), this certificate builds upon the region’s strong sport tourism sector, event venues, recreation economy, and community partnerships.
Furthermore, the certificate dovetails with our broader strategic initiatives in leadership training and workforce development.
The certificate is designed to be stackable: credits may count toward our institution’s MBA or MSM.

It is aimed at working professionals seeking credential rather than comprehensive degree.
While many sport management certificates emphasize marketing or facility operations, ours explicitly integrates leadership and the experience economy.

Yes Fall 2026 Fall 2027 The Organizational Leadership Graduate Certificate provides learners who hold a Bachelor's degree with organizational leadership skills that support career advancement or professional development.
It is designed for working professionals who hold a bachelor’s degree and seek to strengthen their leadership capabilities across a variety of organizational contexts.
Offered fully online, the certificate emphasizes practical leadership, organizational decision making, operations and project management, and the human dynamics of organizations.
Through an interdisciplinary curriculum, students develop skills in leading teams, making informed organizational decisions, managing projects and processes, and navigating ethical, legal, and global considerations.
The certificate supports career advancement, leadership development, and preparation for expanded managerial responsibilities in business, nonprofit, public, and educational organizations.
The Organizational Leadership Graduate Certificate consists of 12 graduate credits.
Program Requirements Students must complete all required courses and one elective course from the approved list below.

The goals of the Organizational Leadership Graduate Certificate are to: Prepare students to lead effectively in diverse organizational settings by developing practical leadership, communication, and collaboration skills.
Strengthen students’ ability to make informed, ethical, and data-driven organizational decisions.
Build competency in managing projects, operations, and organizational processes that support strategic goals.
Enhance understanding of human behavior in organizations, including motivation, talent development, and workforce engagement.
Support career advancement and professional development by aligning leadership education with current and emerging workforce needs.
This program supports Strategy 1 of URI’s Agenda for Change by promoting student success through accessible, high- quality online education; aligning curriculum with workforce and organizational leadership needs; and providing applied, practice-oriented learning that prepares students for leadership roles across business, nonprofit, public, and educational sectors.

In support of the University’s Academic Strategic Plan, the certificate advances student success through flexible, high- quality online education that serves working professionals and adult learners.
The curriculum integrates interdisciplinary perspectives from business, education, and labor relations, reflecting the University’s commitment to collaboration across disciplines and to addressing real-world workforce and organizational needs.
The program further supports the Academic Strategic Plan by strengthening workforce development, enhancing leadership capacity across sectors, and expanding access to graduate credentials that are responsive to regional, national, and global employer demand.
